summary: Iter 51 — Provider Referral $25 Milestone Bonus. Backend: 7/7 pytest pass, covering /api/referrals/me shape (new milestone fields + reward_copy), credit_referrer_milestone unit tests (fires exactly once at 10 paid jobs, idempotent on 11th, no fire under threshold, no fire for non-provider role, no fire without referrer, referral-typed txs don't count), and regression of the 1% per-job commission. Frontend: /wallet renders referral-milestones section with milestone-totals ($0 / 0 paid initially), referral-recruits-empty when no recruits, reward_copy contains '$25' and '10 paid jobs'. /for-providers shows the '$25 referral bonus / Per invited provider' tile in the below-video hints grid.
critical_code_review_comments: credit_referrer_milestone uses a $set-if-not-exists atomic guard via update_one with milestone_10_awarded_at $exists=false — good race protection.

Milestone tx count excludes ref_kind in ['referral', None] — but wallet_transactions rows written without a ref_kind key (e.g. legacy) would also be excluded because $nin treats missing as None. Verified in test_referral_txs_dont_count_toward_milestone. Consider adding an integration test that legacy null-ref_kind rows also don't inflate the count.

In server.py _credit_provider, milestone check is called after inserting the wallet_transactions row on both the stripe_payout and wallet-fallback paths — correct ordering so the 10th row is visible when the count runs.

The 1% per-job credit_referrer runs BEFORE the wallet_transactions row for the current payout is inserted; on the wallet-fallback path this means the milestone check counts the current job (row inserted right after credit_referrer). Consistent for both branches. OK.
referrals.py imports asyncio via 'import asyncio' is not actually used in unit tests file though — cosmetic.
